name: Ethiopia-Eritrea confrontation (Assab and Tigray)
started: 2026-10-01 (diplomatic rupture; Eritrean troops reported in Tigray on 2026-10-07)
summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea broke diplomatic relations on 1 October 2026 amid Ethiopia's war in Tigray. Eritrean troops were reported briefly near Adigrat and hit by Ethiopian drones, and Eritrea says Ethiopia is building a pretext to seize the Red Sea port of Assab.

sides.name: Eritrea
backers: Egypt (diplomatic alignment through the El Alamein declaration; port agreements for Assab, Massawa and Marsa Fatima)
sides.strength: Not public; an Ethiopian official alleged one mechanized and three infantry divisions entered Tigray, which CTP could not corroborate.

background: Ethiopia lost its coastline when Eritrea became independent in 1993, and the two fought a border war in 1998 to 2000. They allied against the TPLF in 2020 to 2022, but Eritrea was left out of the Pretoria agreement. Since 2023 Abiy Ahmed has called Red Sea access an existential 'natural right', which Asmara reads as a threat to Assab.

Egypt, which opposes Ethiopia's Nile dam, has built a bloc with Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan. That matters because a Tigray war on Eritrea's border can now trigger an interstate war with regional backers on both sides.
year: In August 2026 Eritrean officers appeared in Tigray and Eritrea reportedly moved tanks and artillery into southern Tigray. On 25 September Ethiopia's army chief accused Eritrea of financing the TPLF. On 1 October Ethiopia expelled ten Eritrean diplomats and closed its embassy, and Eritrea cut ties, calling it a declaration of war. On 4 October Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan issued the El Alamein declaration, and Egyptian officials told Reuters the four would coordinate militarily if the conflict threatened their borders. On 7 October Eritrean forces were reported moving south of Adigrat; an Ethiopian drone destroyed a truck there, Ethiopia told the UN Security Council it faced an 'all-out invasion', and by 8 October the Eritrean forces had pulled back north.
situation: As of late October 2026 there is no declared war, but no diplomatic channel either. Ethiopian forces now sit on the border at Zalambessa after taking Adigrat, Adwa and Axum, while Eritrean forces have entrenched north of Zalambessa and around Badme and some remain on the Ethiopian side (AFP, 18 Oct). Unverified reports describe an ENDF clash with Eritrean forces near Bure on 11 October and a federal buildup at Bure, Bododa and Elidar on the A1 road toward Assab. On 10 October Eritrea asked the UN Security Council for Chapter VII measures against Ethiopia, and Abiy has again pledged direct sea access.
technical: CTP and ISW geolocated media of suspected Eritrean forces on the Adigrat to Idaga Hamus road and a destroyed truck from an Ethiopian drone strike (7 to 8 Oct 2026).
CTP satellite review found no large-scale Eritrean buildup and assessed an advisory, logistics and light-infantry role rather than an invasion.
Djibouti handled 96.71% of Ethiopia's maritime cargo in the fiscal year to July 2026 and Berbera 2.74%, which is why Assab matters to Addis Ababa.
Egypt signed port and maritime agreements from Dec 2025 to Jul 2026 covering Doraleh (Djibouti) and Assab, Massawa and Marsa Fatima (Eritrea).

After the El Alamein summit (4 Oct 2026), Egyptian officials told Reuters that Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan agreed to coordinate military and intelligence efforts if the conflict threatens their borders.
Ethiopian drones struck suspected Eritrean forces near Adigrat on 7 and 10 Oct 2026; Eritrea then entrenched north of Zalambessa and around Badme (CTP, AFP).
Unverified reports on 12 Oct 2026 described a federal buildup at Bure, Bododa and Elidar on the A1 highway, the direct road from Ethiopia to Assab (CTP).

Escalating legal framing: Ethiopia's foreign minister invoked the right of self-defence in a 7 Oct letter to the UN Security Council; Eritrea asked the Council on 10 Oct for Chapter VII measures, which can include sanctions or force.
casualties: No confirmed interstate casualties; one Ethiopian drone strike on a suspected Eritrean vehicle was geolocated.
displaced: Not applicable separately; see the Tigray war entry.

timeline.event: ENDF chief Birhanu Jula accuses Eritrea of financing the TPLF.
Ethiopia expels ten Eritrean diplomats; Eritrea severs ties.
El Alamein declaration by Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan.
Abiy, reappointed prime minister, pledges direct sea access.
Eritrean troops reported near Adigrat; Ethiopia tells the UN Security Council of an 'all-out invasion'.
Eritrean forces reported withdrawing north of Adigrat.
Eritrea tells the UN Security Council that Ethiopia's actions amount to a declaration of war and asks for Chapter VII measures.
Unverified reports of an ENDF clash with Eritrean forces near Bure and a federal buildup on the A1 toward Assab.
Eritrean forces withdraw through Zalambessa as federal forces reach the border.

outlook: The key signals are any federal assault on the Adwa and Adigrat area, Eritrean mobilization along the border or toward Afar, Ethiopian moves near Assab, and whether Egypt turns its coordination pledge into military support.

zones.name: Assab
zones.note: Eritrean Red Sea port at the centre of Ethiopia's sea-access demands.

zones.name: Adigrat and Zalambessa border area
zones.note: Where Eritrean troops were reported on 7 Oct 2026.

zones.name: Northern Afar border (approx)
zones.note: Reported Eritrean deployments near the Afar border and ARDUF activity toward Dalol.

zones.name: Bure front on the A1 to Assab (approx)
zones.note: Unverified reports of a federal troop and heavy-weapons buildup at Bure, Bododa and Elidar and a clash near Bure on 11 Oct 2026.

zones.name: Badme (approx)
zones.note: Disputed town from the 1998 to 2000 war; Eritrean forces reported entrenched around it in Oct 2026.

battles.name: Adigrat front and reported Eritrean incursion
battles.place: Adigrat, Idaga Hamus and Zalambessa, Tigray, Ethiopia
battles.outcome: Eritrean forces reported moving south of Adigrat withdrew north after Ethiopian drone strikes on 7 and 10 Oct; ENDF and TPF took Atsbi, Hawzen, Freweyni and Idaga Hamus, entered Adigrat without resistance on 9 to 10 Oct and reached the border at Zalambessa on 12 Oct as Eritrean units pulled back through it.
battles.forces: Ethiopian official claimed one mechanized and three infantry Eritrean divisions; a foreign security source told AFP Eritrea deployed thousands of troops; CTP found no large buildup in satellite imagery.
battles.losses: One Eritrean truck destroyed by an Ethiopian drone (geolocated by CTP and ISW); no other figures.
battles.significance: The closest the two states have come to direct combat since 2000, leaving Ethiopian and Eritrean troops facing each other at Zalambessa and Badme.
